contains: Sorting Room

Pigeonholes climb every wall of the depot, each one stencilled with the name of a world: Ceres, Titan, Kepler Station, places you have only seen as postmarks. The sorting machine hums in the middle of the floor. East, the loading dock door is shut.
Sorting Room

Pigeonholes climb every wall of the depot, each one stencilled with the name of a world: Ceres, Titan, Kepler Station, places you have only seen as postmarks. The sorting machine hums in the middle of the floor. East, the loading dock door is shut.
You put on the mail satchel.
The sorting machine is fixed in place.
A squat steel cabinet the size of a shuttle engine, chuckling to itself as it reads addresses. Its out tray is empty for now.
ROUTE 7: Ceres, Titan, Kepler Station. Return to depot when empty.
The sorting machine pauses mid-chuckle, then goes on without you.
The sorting machine takes that as addressed to it, and files it.
The sorting machine takes that as addressed to it, and files it.
There is nothing to apologize for.
You wave. Nobody waves back.
You find nothing under the sorting machine.
The mail satchel is already empty.
You kiss the sorting machine. Nothing comes of it.
You wave the route card about. Nothing happens.
You take the dead letter from the returns bin.
You toss the dead letter to the ground.
Taken.
The sorting machine snatches the letter out of the air, reads the address, finds no world by that name, and spits it back onto the floor.
Taken.
The dead letter skims across the floor and drops into the returns bin as if it knew the way.
You find nothing under the returns bin.
You empty the returns bin onto the floor: a dead letter.
The sorting machine stops chuckling for a moment, as if it had been counting on that one.
The returns bin is already empty.
The disposal torch isn't something you can burn.
You need the disposal torch to burn the dead letter.
Taken.
The dead letter goes up in a flat orange sheet and is gone before the smell reaches you.
Dropped.
The disposal torch isn't for sale.
You buy the ration bar.
The kiosk counts your credits twice, grudgingly, and lets go of what you paid for.
You can't afford the flask of coffee.
You already have the ration bar.
The loading dock door stays shut until your shift is cleared to launch.
The sorting machine gives a satisfied clunk. On the east wall, the panel beside the dock door flips from red to green, and the door rolls up into the ceiling.
Dropped.
Loading Dock

A hangar of cold air and sodium light. The courier ship squats on its skids in the middle of the bay, its boarding ramp drawn up tight. A loader robot waits beside the ramp, and empty mail crates are stacked along the west wall. The depot is back through the door to the west.
Your boots ring on the deck plates. Somewhere above, a fan the size of a house turns over once and stops.
Dust, a bent staple, and the floor.
The loader's status light goes red, then amber again. It has filed a report.
The ramp is the loader's to work, and the loader does not take requests from carriers.
The ramp is the loader's to work, and the loader does not take requests from carriers.
You can't lower the mail crates.
The Sparrow's ramp stays up. The loader robot's amber light blinks at you, patient as a clock.
A snub-nosed UPPS courier, the Sparrow, dented along one flank where some asteroid got the last word. Its boarding ramp is drawn up, and the hull plating is cold to the touch.

Pigeonholes climb every wall of the depot, each one stencilled with the name of a world: Ceres, Titan, Kepler Station, places you have only seen as postmarks. The sorting machine hums in the middle of the floor. East, the loading dock door is shut.
Loading Dock

A hangar of cold air and sodium light. The courier ship squats on its skids in the middle of the bay, its boarding ramp drawn up tight. A loader robot waits beside the ramp, and empty mail crates are stacked along the west wall. The depot is back through the door to the west.
The route card is the one thing on this dock that is yours to keep.
The satchel stays on your shoulder. A carrier without a satchel is just somebody in grey.

The loader robot unfolds its arms, takes the bundle as gently as an egg, and rolls to the Sparrow. The ramp comes down with a hiss of hydraulics, and the robot trundles up it and back out, empty. Its brow light turns green.
Hold

The Sparrow's hold, a steel room no wider than a corridor, ribbed with cargo netting. A suit locker stands bolted to the aft bulkhead, and a ladder climbs to the cockpit hatch at the forward end. The ramp slopes down to the dock.
You can see a suit locker, a specimen jar, a coil of strapping, and a mail bundle here.
The cockpit hatch is dogged shut, and the placard says why.

You open the suit locker.

In the suit locker you see a space suit.
You put on the space suit.
PRE-FLIGHT COMPLETE
